Subject: Checkout failures & p99 spike after SDK 2.1.0 rollout

Hi Rachel —

We rolled SDK 2.1.0 for our mobile checkout yesterday (gradual rollout to 10% traffic) and immediately saw p99 latency for tokenization and several 502/504s on our checkout route. By morning the spike was impacting ~7% of transactions and our conversion dropped.

Attached are a short trace (quickcart-p99-sample-trace.log) and a pcap snippet. The errors look like sudden stalls during the streaming response — client reports show "stream closed before headers" and occasional duplicated header lines.

Can Redwood confirm whether anything on your side changed around framing/headers or if this is likely an SDK integration edge-case? We need an ETA — this is customer-impacting.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Checkout failures & p99 spike after SDK 2.1.0 rollout

Rach / Marissa / Alex (cc'd by Rachel) —

Thanks for the traces. Initial triage notes below (runtime team):

Summary of findings (preliminary):
- The pcap shows multiple tiny frames where header blocks are split across fragments; our streaming parser in the gateway currently expects a conservative header reassembly boundary and, under heavy concurrency, can stall waiting for a trailing frame that sometimes gets reordered by some mobile network middleboxes.
- SDK 2.1.0 introduced an experimental "aggressive keepalive" which reduces network-level coalescing; in combo with flaky middleboxes, this increases the chance of header split/reorder and trips a code path in our parser that currently retries synchronously, raising latency and occasionally returning a 502 when the parser gives up.

Immediate mitigations we can push TODAY: 
1) Deploy a hotfix to the gateway parser to tolerate out-of-order header fragments by using a small reassembly buffer and async reordering (rollout to edge nodes only). Target: 4-6 hour rollout.
2) Recommend QuickCart temporarily pin client rollout to 2.0.7 while we validate the fix.
3) Add a short-term server-side proxy rule to increase upstream read timeout by 250ms for affected routes (non-invasive).

Longer-term: improve parser robustness and add telemetry to detect header-fragment anomalies; coordinate an SDK tweak to back off the aggressive keepalive unless the network path advertises support.

I'll start a hotfix branch now and share a deploy plan. Need permission to escalate to infra for immediate edge push.

-Karthik
